steps.title: Initial Sample Preparation
steps.instruction: Prepare the initial sample by heating and cooling.

substeps.instruction: Heat at 70°C for 2 minutes in a heat block, then immediately place on ice.
Incubate on ice for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Prepare Reaction Mix
steps.instruction: Combine reagents for each sample in a nuclease-free, low binding PCR tube on ice.

substeps.instruction: Mix reagents until visibly homogenous by pipetting.
Briefly centrifuge to collect contents at the bottom of the tube.

steps.title: First Incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate the reaction at 25°C for 2 hours in a thermocycler with the lid left open.

substeps.instruction: 30 minutes before the end of incubation, place NEXTflex™ Cleanup Beads (BROWN CAP) at room temperature.

steps.title: Excess 3' Adapter Removal (Step B)
steps.instruction: Remove excess 3' adapters using depletion solution and beads.

substeps.instruction: Add 25 μL of NEXTflex™ Adapter Depletion Solution to each sample, mix well by pipetting, and transfer the entire sample to a new nuclease-free, low binding microcentrifuge tube.
Add 40 μL of properly resuspended, room temperature equilibrated NEXTflex™ Cleanup Beads (vortexed for at least 30 seconds) and mix well by pipetting.
Immediately add 60 μL of isopropanol and mix well by pipetting.
Incubate for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Magnetize samples until the solution appears clear (2-5 minutes).
Remove and save supernatant in a new tube for recovery (Note 17).
While on the magnet, add 180 μL of freshly prepared 80% ethanol, incubate for 30 seconds, and remove supernatant. Repeat for a total of 2 ethanol washes.
Incubate on the magnet for 3 minutes: after 1 minute, remove tubes and briefly centrifuge to collect residual ethanol, then replace on magnet for the final 2 minutes.
Remove all residual liquid from the bottom of the well with a pipette.
Remove sample from magnetic stand and resuspend bead pellet in 22 μL of Resuspension Buffer by pipetting.
Incubate for 2 minutes at room temperature.
Magnetize samples until the solution appears clear (2-5 minutes).
Transfer 20 μL of supernatant to a new microcentrifuge tube and save (do not discard).

steps.title: Second Adapter Depletion
steps.instruction: Perform a second round of adapter depletion on the saved supernatant.

substeps.instruction: Add 25 μL of NEXTflex Adapter Depletion Solution to the 20 μL of supernatant and mix well by pipetting.
Add 40 μL of properly resuspended, room temperature equilibrated NEXTflex Cleanup Beads and mix well by pipetting.
Immediately add 60 μL of isopropanol and mix well by pipetting.
Incubate for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Magnetize samples until the solution appears clear (2-5 minutes).
Remove and save supernatant in a new tube for recovery.
While on the magnet, add 180 μL of freshly prepared 80% ethanol, incubate for 30 seconds, and remove supernatant. Repeat for a total of 2 ethanol washes.
Incubate on the magnet for 3 minutes: after 1 minute, remove tubes and briefly centrifuge to collect residual ethanol, then replace on magnet for the final 2 minutes.
Remove all residual liquid from the bottom of the well with a pipette.
Remove tubes from magnetic stand and resuspend bead pellet in 13 μL of Nuclease-free water by pipetting.
Incubate for 2 minutes at room temperature.
Magnetize samples until the solution appears clear (2-5 minutes).
Transfer 11.5 μL of supernatant to a new low binding PCR tube.

steps.title: Excess Adapter Inactivation (Step C)
steps.instruction: Inactivate excess adapters using a specific thermocycler program.

substeps.instruction: Mix samples thoroughly by pipetting and briefly centrifuge.
Set thermocycler lid to 60°C but leave it open during the 12°C incubation; close it for the 50°C incubation.
Keep samples on ice until the PCR block reaches 12°C, then transfer tubes to the thermocycler.

steps.title: NEXTflex 5' 4N Adapter Ligation (Step D)
steps.instruction: Ligate the 5' 4N adapter to the samples.

substeps.instruction: Heat 1.5 μL of NEXTflex 5' 4N adapter per reaction at 70°C for 2 minutes in a heat block, then immediately place on ice.
Combine reagents on ice in a nuclease-free, low binding PCR tube, mixing until visibly homogenous by pipetting or brief vortexing.
Incubate at 20°C for 1 hour in a thermocycler with the lid left open.

steps.title: Reverse Transcription - First Strand Synthesis (Step E)
steps.instruction: Synthesize the first strand of cDNA.

substeps.instruction: Mix thoroughly by pipetting and briefly centrifuge.
Incubate on a thermocycler with lid temperature of 100°C: 30 min at 42°C and 10 min at 90°C.
Spin tubes down to collect condensed droplets from lids.

steps.title: Bead Cleanup (Step F)
steps.instruction: Clean up the first strand synthesis product using beads.

substeps.instruction: Add 20 μL of room temperature equilibrated NEXTflex™ Cleanup Beads to 40 μL of First Strand Synthesis product, mix well, and transfer to a low binding microcentrifuge tube.
Add 22 μL isopropanol and mix well by pipetting.
Incubate for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Magnetize samples until the solution appears clear (2-5 minutes).
Transfer 70 μL of supernatant (containing cDNA) to a new low binding microcentrifuge tube; do not transfer beads.
Add 10 μL NEXTflex™ Adapter Depletion Solution to the supernatant and mix well by pipetting.
Add 20 μL of resuspended room temperature NEXTflex Cleanup Beads and mix well by pipetting.
Add 68 μL of isopropanol and mix well by pipetting.
Incubate for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Magnetize samples until the solution appears clear (2-5 minutes).
Remove and save supernatant in a new tube for recovery.
While on the magnet, add 180 μL of freshly prepared 80% ethanol, incubate for 30 seconds, and remove supernatant. Repeat for a total of 2 ethanol washes.
Incubate on the magnet for 3 minutes: after 1 minute, remove tubes and briefly centrifuge to collect residual ethanol, then replace on magnet for the final 2 minutes.
Remove all residual liquid from the bottom of the well with a pipette.
Remove sample from magnetic stand and resuspend bead pellet in 20 μL Nuclease-free Water by pipetting.
Incubate for 2 minutes at room temperature.
Magnetize samples until the solution appears clear (2-5 minutes).
Transfer 18 μL of supernatant to a new low binding PCR tube.

steps.title: PCR Amplification (Step G)
steps.instruction: Amplify the library via PCR and analyze the products.

substeps.instruction: Perform PCR amplification.
Analyze products via Agilent Bioanalyzer HS DNA Assay (1 μL diluted 1/4 with water) or 6% TBE-PAGE gel (5 μL product + 1 μL 6x Loading Dye).
If a strong ~150 bp band is present and no ~130 bp band (adapter dimer) is detected, proceed to Step H1 (Gel-Free).
If a strong ~150 bp band and an ~130 bp band are both present, proceed to Step H2 (PAGE Selection).

steps.title: Option H1: Gel-Free Size Selection Cleanup
steps.instruction: Perform size selection using a bead-based method.

substeps.instruction: Ensure PCR product volume is exactly 25 μL (add Nuclease-free Water if necessary).
Add 32.5 μL of resuspended, room temperature equilibrated NEXTflex™ Cleanup Beads and mix well by pipetting.
Incubate for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Magnetize samples until the solution appears clear (2-5 minutes).
Transfer 52.5 μL of supernatant to a new nuclease-free, low binding microcentrifuge tube (do not discard).
Add 30 μL of resuspended, room temperature equilibrated NEXTflex Cleanup Beads to the supernatant and mix well by pipetting.
Incubate for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Magnetize samples until the solution appears clear (2-5 minutes).
Remove and save supernatant in a new tube for recovery.
While on the magnet, add 180 μL of freshly prepared 80% ethanol, incubate for 30 seconds, and remove supernatant. Repeat for a total of 2 ethanol washes.
Incubate on the magnet for 3 minutes: after 1 minute, remove tubes and briefly centrifuge to collect residual ethanol, then replace on magnet for the final 2 minutes.
Remove all residual liquid from the bottom of the well with a pipette.
Remove samples from magnetic stand and resuspend bead pellet in 13.5 μL of Resuspension Buffer by pipetting.
Incubate for 2 minutes at room temperature.
Magnetize samples until the solution appears clear (2-5 minutes).
Transfer 12 μL of supernatant to a new low binding microcentrifuge tube as the final sequencing library.
Verify size distribution via Bioanalyzer HS DNA Assay and concentration via Qubit dsDNA HS Assay.

steps.title: Option H2: PAGE Size Selection and Cleanup
steps.instruction: Perform size selection using a TBE-PAGE gel.

substeps.instruction: Add 5 μL of 6X Gel Loading Dye to 25 μL of PCR product and mix well.
Load samples onto a 6% TBE-PAGE gel, leaving 1-2 lanes between samples of the same barcode; load 10 μL of Ready to Load Low MW Ladder in an adjacent lane.
Run the gel with 1X TBE buffer at 200 V for approximately 30 minutes until the lower dye band is 0.5-1 cm from the bottom.
Visualize bands on a UV transilluminator; use a clean razor to cut out the ~150 bp band (avoid the ~130 bp band) and place in a 1.7 mL nuclease-free, low binding microcentrifuge tube.
Briefly centrifuge the tube and crush the gel slice thoroughly with a disposable pestle.
Add 300 μL of NEXTflex™ Elution Buffer, remove the pestle, and soak for at least 2 hours or overnight at room temperature with agitation.
Pulse spin tubes to collect eluate from walls and lid.
Add 50 μL of resuspended room temperature NEXTflex Cleanup Beads and 350 μL of isopropanol; mix well by pipetting.
Incubate at room temperature for 10 minutes (agitation recommended).
Pulse spin tubes to collect solution and pellet beads.
Magnetize samples until the solution appears clear (2-5 minutes).
Remove and save supernatant in a new tube for recovery.
Add 950 μL 80% ethanol, incubate for 30 seconds, and remove supernatant. Repeat for a total of 2 ethanol washes.
Incubate on the magnet for 3 minutes: after 1 minute, remove tubes and briefly centrifuge to collect residual ethanol, then replace on magnet for the final 2 minutes.
Remove all residual liquid from the bottom of the well with a pipette.
Remove samples from magnetic stand and resuspend bead pellet in 13 μL of Resuspension Buffer by pipetting.
Incubate for 2 minutes at room temperature.
Magnetize samples until the solution appears clear (2-5 minutes).
Transfer 12 μL of supernatant to a clean nuclease-free, low binding microcentrifuge tube as the final sequencing library.
Verify size distribution via Bioanalyzer HS DNA Assay and concentration via Qubit dsDNA HS Assay.

description: Approximate time to complete: 2.5 hours Background: The 3' 4N adenylated adapter is a population of DNA oligonucleotides identical to each other but for the 4 nucleotides at the 5' terminal which are degenerate (4N) . This design ameliorates the inherent base-specific biases of RNA ligase, thus allowing more accurate representation of the bonafide relative quatities of a sample's small RNA species in the final sequencing library. Click on the following link to access the publication demonstrating the effectiveness of this pooling strategy: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC3241666/ The ligase used in this reaction is a truncated form of T4 RNA ligase 2 (Rnl2), which lacks adenylation activity, but maintains its ligase functionality. Also, unlike its full length counterpart, this truncated ligase cannot ligate the phosphorylated 5' end of DNA or RNA to the 3' end of RNA. It will ligate only a 5'-end pre-adenylated substrate (DNA or RNA) to the 3' end of an RNA molecule. As such, RNA molecules from the input sample will not be adenylated and thus themselves become substrates for ligation. This prevents circularization or concatenation of input RNA, and specifies the ligation of the adenylated adapter to the 3' end of the input RNA molecules. Furthermore, the 3' 4N adapters possess at their 3' end a dideoxy nucleotide, thus preventing its ligation to the 5' end of the input RNA, and also to itself. Figure 2 below shows the final products of this step.
